competitors.name: CircleUp
competitors.what: Equity platform linking accredited investors with consumer and retail companies
competitors.traction_then: Launched April 2012; no traction figures in the source

target_customer: Startups raising small amounts from many investors, and everyday (including non-accredited) investors
problem: Only accredited investors could buy startup equity; JOBS Act (2012) was expected to let anyone invest small amounts.

founders.name: Nick Tommarello
founders.background_notes: Grew up in rural upstate New York; father was a serial entrepreneur who went bankrupt several times (Tommarello interview quoted by Mercury). Founding date differs by source (see notes).

founders.name: Mike Norman
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on Wikipedia only (marked citation needed); Medium/search snippets name Tommarello and Belote.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web platform with legal/escrow workflow; regulation more than technology was the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Registration as funding portal and investor/startup two-sided network are hard to replicate quickly; not evidenced with sources read.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Wefunder. A 2025 Crowdfund Insider piece reports StartEngine bought SeedInvest, and Wefunder predicts industry consolidation with StartEngine as the likely other survivor (search snippet, page returned 403).

market_need_then: The JOBS Act was signed 5 April 2012 and promised equity crowdfunding for non-accredited investors, but Title III rules were still pending in April 2013 and SEC proposals came late 2013 (Fortune and other 2013 coverage found in search snippets). Demand was regulatory and speculative at founding.

identity.logo: Wordmark with a W mark (shown on aggregator pages; no description found)
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven and populist ('anyone can invest $100'; 'army of people who care')

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: everyone can invest $100 in startups they care about

rebrands.why: Tommarello said he disliked the phrase 'crowdfunding' and that the industry had the right to rename it (Crowdfund Insider, via search snippet; this renames the product category, not the company)

branding.community_and_virality: Large retail investor community; claims thousands of small investors backing its own raise (secondary sources, unverified). Runs a public impact report (Crowdfund Insider).

brand_strength.rationale: Became the best-known name in US equity crowdfunding, with roughly a third of Reg CF capital by one secondary review (unverified), and a clear mission message; no independent brand study found, so the rating rests on market position.

outcome_analysis: Wefunder, YC W13, bet on the JOBS Act and then waited years for the Reg CF rules (effective 2016) before the market opened. It has since become one of the largest Reg CF portals, with secondary sources putting cumulative volume near $1B and about a third of Reg CF capital, though these are unverified. A May 2022 FINRA letter says it raised about $20M above the Reg CF cap across 39 offerings in 2016-21, a compliance setback rather than a failure. Still Active with about 35 staff; no exit.
notes: Funding of Wefunder itself: aggregator figures conflict (CB Insights $30.9M over 21 rounds, PremierAlts $69.4M; a tear sheet lists a Jun 2021 Reg CF round of $8.99M and a 2025 community round, a 2021 Series A at $160M post), none confirmed in a primary source or second outlet; Form D data found relates to separate Wefunds vehicles. Recorded as none_found, not zero. Crowdfund Insider pages returned 403 (not worked around). Fundable and Crowdfunder (both launched May 2012, per search snippets) are not listed because the dated source was not opened. Volume figures ($983M, $109M in 2025) and the $1.4M FINRA fine come from an affiliate-style review and are unverified; the FINRA letter itself is cited. Wikipedia says founded 2012 (citation needed), YC page and infobox say 2011; one search snippet says June 2012. Name origin not found. A second search confirmed rounds exist (CB Insights lists many; a 2019 Series A of about 1.7M was reported by Crunchbase) but amounts and dates conflict and no page with a specific round was opened, so none recorded. Mike Norman is already listed as co-founder.
